stemBlocks.value: Think first: A negative index is handled by the same addition and subtraction rules as a positive one.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p064-q17 from workbook page 64.

solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply the coefficients in the numerator.
Add the indices in the numerator.
Write the negative index as a fraction.

strategyBlocks.value: Combine the numerator by adding indices, divide by the denominator by subtracting indices, then rewrite the negative index as a fraction.

whyThisWorks.value: The index laws are defined so that they keep working when the index is negative or zero. A negative index simply records division rather than multiplication, so x⁻⁶ means 1/x⁶. Because the rules extend consistently, you can add and subtract the indices exactly as usual and only convert to a fraction at the very end.

commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding 2 and 5 instead of 2 and −5.

commonErrors.misconception: Moving the whole term, coefficient included, into the denominator to give 1/(2x⁶).

examTip.value: Keep the indices negative through the working and convert to a fraction only in the final line; converting early makes the subtraction step much harder to control.
